42959416.titulo: An integrated One Health methodology to study Rift Valley fever, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever and brucellosis at the human-livestock-wildlife interface in Uganda.
42959416.autores: Kizito D, Tweed S, … Lutwama JJ (29 autores)
42959416.resumo: Zoonotic diseases pose a significant public health challenge, with most emerging diseases originating from animal populations. In Uganda, Rift Valley fever (RVF), Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF) and brucellosis are endemic, yet critical gaps remain in understanding their transmission dynamics, key vectors and reservoirs, environmental drivers, community knowledge and behaviours and the implementation of One Health policies. The Collaborative One Health Research Initiative on Epidemics-Uganda (COHRIE-Uganda) study developed an integrated, interdisciplinary approach to investigate these diseases across ecologically diverse areas characterised by intense human-livestock-wildlife interaction. The study methodology comprised sequential cross-sectional surveys combining quantitative and qualitative methods, involving community members, livestock, wildlife and vectors across six conservation areas in Uganda. Household surveys and blood sampling were obtained from 3018 individuals and 35 focus group discussions were conducted across 96 villages. 67 in-depth interviews with community leaders and 26 interviews with national policymakers were conducted to evaluate One Health policy implementation. Livestock practices were assessed through farmer questionnaires and blood sampling of 2199 cattle, 343 sheep, 78 pigs and 1582 goats. Invertebrate vector sampling was undertaken of 72,744 mosquitoes and 9273 ticks on livestock hosts with vertebrate host sampling of 612 small mammals. 233 large wildlife were sampled by blood and nasal swabs. Real-time monitoring and detection of zoonotic outbreaks was provided by 127 trained Community One Health Volunteers embedded at each site. COHRIE-Uganda presents a novel interdisciplinary methodology to study zoonotic disease, applying a One Health approach integrating molecular epidemiology, ecology, social sciences and community participatory methods involving humans, livestock, vectors, and wildlife to inform culturally sensitive zoonotic disease interventions.

42956390.titulo: Establishing Potosi Virus as a Human Pathogen: Fatal Neuroinvasive Disease in a B-Cell-Depleted Patient.
42956390.autores: Abbatemarco JR, Begum F, … Fox RJ (22 autores)
42956390.resumo:
To establish Potosi virus, a mosquito-borne member of the family Peribunyaviridae, as a neuroinvasive human pathogen.
Case report.
A 37-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis on long-term rituximab developed rapidly progressive dementia. Serial MRI demonstrated progressive generalized atrophy. CSF showed transient, minimal lymphocytic pleocytosis. Extensive infectious, autoimmune, and prion evaluations were unrevealing, but CSF metagenomic sequencing detected all 3 genome segments for Potosi virus. Postmortem examination revealed diffuse meningoencephalitis with T-cell-predominant leptomeningeal and perivascular inflammation. Molecular analyses confirmed multiple nucleotide sequences with >99+% concordance with a known Potosi strain, with widespread viral infection confirmed by immunohistochemistry demonstrating intracellular and extracellular viral antigen. Electron microscopy demonstrated particles of a size consistent with the Peribunyaviridae family. Metagenomic sequencing of RNA extracted from frozen brain tissue identified all 3 Potosi virus gene segments without other infectious entities. Findings were concordant across multiple laboratories and institutions.
Potosi virus can cause fatal neuroinvasive disease in humans, as evidenced by convergent postmortem neuropathologic, molecular, and ultrastructural evidence. Chronic B-cell depletion may increase susceptibility to severe disease with arboviral infections, which may present without conventional CNS inflammatory markers. CSF metagenomic sequencing should be considered in immunocompromised patients with unexplained progressive neurologic decline.

42958790.titulo: Assessing the Relative Contribution of Pre-Deployment Abroad Versus In-Mission Dirofilaria immitis Infections in French Military Working Dogs Screened Post-Mission: A Quantitative Risk Assessment.
42958790.autores: Grosbois A, Risco-Castillo V, … Crozet G (4 autores)
42958790.revista: Risk analysis : an official publication of the Society for Risk Analysis
42958790.resumo: Dirofilaria immitis (D. immitis) is a mosquito-borne nematode responsible for canine cardiopulmonary dirofilariasis, a parasitic infection widely distributed worldwide and established in mainland France, particularly in southern regions. Military working dogs (MWDs) may be at increased risk of exposure to vector-borne pathogens because of their predominantly outdoor lifestyle and frequent missions abroad. Nevertheless, D. immitis infection remains sporadic in this population, likely due to well-implemented medical prophylaxis. The aim of this study was to investigate the likely origin of D. immitis infections detected in MWD during post-mission screening using a quantitative risk analysis approach. Scenario trees were developed to describe the sequences of events leading to the return of an infected dog from a mission abroad, accounting for parasite biology, prophylactic measures, and compliance. The model estimated a mean annual number of 4.25 infected MWD returning from missions out of an average annual population of 466 returning dogs, of which 79% were detected through post-mission screening. Most infections were likely acquired before deployment, either during previous missions, at the breeding facility before purchase, or within mainland France. Only 7.9% of infections acquired during missions were expected to be detected by testing performed at the end of the post-mission quarantine period. Alternative scenarios highlighted the effectiveness of chemoprophylaxis, as its absence was associated with a 3.2-fold increase in the number of infected dogs. Simulations also showed that extending the interval between return and testing would substantially improve the detection of mission-acquired infections. These findings support the continued use of preventive measures while questioning the adequacy of current post-mission screening alone for identifying D. immitis infections acquired during deployment.

42954423.titulo: Introduction and Spread of West Nile Virus in Lazio, Italy, 2025: Molecular Epidemiology and Genomic Characterization.
42954423.autores: Rueca M, Gruber CEM, … Carletti F (23 autores)
42954423.resumo: West Nile virus (WNV) is a flavivirus whose cycle involves mosquitoes and avian hosts that occasionally may infect horses and humans as "dead-end hosts." Human infection is mostly asymptomatic, sometimes leading to febrile or neuroinvasive disease. In 2025, Italy experienced its largest epidemic with an unprecedented geographic spread (79 provinces; 52% of cases in central Italy). Here we report whole‑genome sequencing and phylogeographic analysis of 39 WNV lineage 2 samples collected in Lazio and Campania regions between July and September 2025 from humans and animal samples. All 2025 strains belonged to a Southern Italian clade that diversified around 2020, with evidence of earlier circulation in 2024. All the 2025 genomes shared a substitution that lies in envelope protein domain III (K399R), potentially influencing interactions with the viral membrane. The same mutation was previously detected in Eastern European strains, leading to the hypothesis of introductions in Italy via migratory birds from these regions. Phylogeography identified strong viral dispersal routes within Central Italy supporting a pattern of short‑range spread and local overwintering. Overall, results highlight the roles of ecological conditions and cross‑border transmission dynamics in shaping the 2025 Italian epidemic, underscoring the need for integrated genomic/ecological surveillance.

42962859.titulo: The EF1A2-PABP-E75 axis coordinates metabolic reprogramming and 20E-dependent reproduction in the mosquito Aedes aegypti.
42962859.autores: Lou Y, Wei T, … Liu S (9 autores)
42962859.resumo: Ovarian development and reproductive maturation in Aedes aegypti critically depend on 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) signaling and energy metabolic homeostasis. Knockdown of EF1A2 (AAEL017096) profoundly affects lipid nutrient metabolism in the fat body and ovarian development, yet whether this effect involves 20E signaling has remained unclear. Here, we show that EF1A2 silencing significantly suppresses transcription of the Halloween genes CYP314A1, CYP315A1, and CYP307A1, reduces endogenous 20E titers, and blocks downstream hormonal signaling. Differential proteomic analysis reveals that EF1A2 broadly participates in metabolic reprogramming, endoplasmic reticulum protein processing, and mRNA regulation. The poly(A)-binding protein PABP (AAEL010318) is identified as a core downstream effector and is specifically highly expressed in ovaries of post-blood-meal mosquitoes. PABP knockdown causes aberrant lipid accumulation in the fat body, disrupts glycolipid metabolism, and ultimately arrests ovarian development and impairs reproductive output, recapitulating EF1A2 knockdown phenotypes. Mechanistically, EF1A2 directly binds full-length PABP via its domain I, positively regulating PABP protein abundance. PABP regulates transcription of the Halloween genes CYP302A1, CYP306A1, and CYP315A1, thereby modulating 20E titer and, in turn, Vg transcription. PABP also associates with the 3' UTR of E75 mRNA, stabilizing the transcript and activating downstream 20E signaling. E75 positively regulates CYP302A1, CYP306A1, and CYP314A1 through a positive feedback mechanism; E75 downregulation impairs ovarian development and reduces egg production. Collectively, the EF1A2-PABP-E75 axis coordinates hormone biosynthesis and metabolic homeostasis to sustain ovarian development and reproductive capacity, offering molecular targets for mosquito vector control.

42962057.titulo: Epidemiological characteristics and transmission dynamics of dengue in Ningbo City, China before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic interventions.
42962057.autores: Chu Y, Zhao Y, … Chen Y (10 autores)
42962057.resumo:
Ningbo experienced a local dengue outbreak in 2018-2019, followed by the implementation and relaxation of COVID-19 pandemic interventions. Evidence has been limited on dengue epidemiology and the transmissibility across these periods.
We analyzed routine dengue cases and mosquito surveillance data from 2017 to 2024, using descriptive analyses to assess the epidemiological characteristics, and a mathematical model was developed to estimate the basic reproduction number (R0).
A total of 266 dengue cases were reported, with no deaths. Before the pandemic interventions, 51.19% of cases were overseas-imported; no cases were reported during pandemic interventions, whereas 73.47% were domestically imported after pandemic interventions. The median age of cases was 38.50 years (IQR = 31.25-54.00), and 57.52% were unemployed, retired, or in commercial services. The onset-to-diagnosis interval shortened post-interventions (4.46 days vs. 2.67 days). Viral typing increased post-interventions (34.59% vs. 63.27%), with 83.70% of cases identified as dengue virus-1 infections. Dengue cases were reported across all districts, with higher proportions in Haishu (27.07%) and Yinzhou (24.44%). The incidence was 2.82 per 100,000 persons. Incidence did not differ significantly by sex, but was significantly higher among individuals 15-59 years and those aged ≥60years than among those aged ≤14 years (3.18 and 3.01 per 100,000 persons, respectively, vs. 0.45 per 100,000 persons). Incidence was highest in Haishu and Jiangbei (6.90 and 4.93 per 100,000 persons, respectively). A post-intervention incidence rebound was observed, although no statistically significant differences were observed in the ≤ 14 age group, Beilun District, Ninghai County and Xiangshan County. Aedes albopictus was the only vector species. The mean Breteau Index was 16.07 (SD: 8.04) and decreased across phases, and rebounded in Jiangbei, Zhenhai, and Haishu districts. The mean BI was higher in summer compared to other seasons (p < 0.05). Model fit was strong (R2 > 0.95). The median R0 was higher in the outbreak years (3.46, IQR = 2.98-3.95) than years without local transmission (0.00, IQR = 0.00-0.00; p < 0.001). Median R0 was 0.00 (IQR = 0.00-0.71) over 2017-2024 due to the absence of local cases in most years.
Dengue remains non-endemic in Ningbo, and is driven primarily by imported infections rather than sustained local transmission. Despite a reduction in diagnostic delay and vector density, post-PHSM incidences rebounded, and district-level heterogeneity indicates ongoing outbreak potential. Sustained surveillance, rapid diagnosis and district-tailored vector control are critical to prevent re-establishment of local transmission.

42961998.titulo: Functional dissection of conserved RNAi pathways in antiviral immunity of several hemipteran insects.
42961998.autores: Zhang Y, Ye ZX, … Li JM (9 autores)
42961998.resumo: The small silencing RNA pathways are crucial post-transcriptional gene silencing mechanisms involved in antiviral defense, gene regulation, and transposon suppression. In insects, the three main pathways are the microRNA (miRNA), Piwi-interacting RNA (piRNA), and small interfering RNA (siRNA) pathways. While these pathways are well-studied in model insects like fruit flies and mosquitoes (Order: Diptera), their functions in non-model insects remain largely unexplored. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive functional screening of core RNAi-related genes in a hemipteran insect, the small brown planthopper (Laodelphax striatellus). Our results demonstrated that genes in the miRNA pathway (AGO1 and DCR1) and the piRNA pathway (Piwi and AGO3) are essential for the survival, development, and fecundity of L. striatellus, but they are not actively involved in the antiviral response. Unexpectedly, knocking down the key siRNA pathway gene DCR2 did not produce a detectable change in viral accumulation or the abundance of virus-derived small interfering RNAs. This finding suggests that substantial depletion of DCR2 does not detectably impair the measured antiviral siRNA responses in L. striatellus under our experimental conditions. A similar lack of detectable antiviral phenotypes following DCR2 knockdown was observed in three other representative hemipteran insects from different families/genera (Sogatella furcifera, Nilaparvata lugens, and Bemisia tabaci). Additionally, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of DCR2 resulted in embryonic lethality in homozygous mutant strains of L. striatellus, while heterozygous mutants showed significantly prolonged developmental duration. Functional RNAi-of-RNAi assays further demonstrated that DCR2 pre-knockdown did not detectably reduce silencing of a subsequently introduced dsRNA reporter in L. striatellus, and DCR2-heterozygous mutants with reduced DCR2 expression showed no change in viral accumulation. These results reveal an essential developmental role for DCR2 and indicate that partial DCR2 depletion does not measurably compromise antiviral immunity under the tested conditions. Collectively, our findings broaden our understanding of the organization and biological functions of small silencing RNA pathways in hemipteran insects.

42961996.titulo: High quality chromosomal genome assemblies of three human Plasmodium species directly from natural infections.
42961996.autores: Dogga SK, Rop JC, … Lawniczak MKN (16 autores)
42961996.resumo: Malaria, caused by mosquito-transmitted Plasmodium parasites, remains a major global health challenge. While P. falciparum accounts for most malaria deaths, the lesser-studied P. ovale spp. and P. malariae also contribute to disease burden across many endemic regions, typically causing milder but chronic infections. Here, we generated high quality, chromosome-level reference genomes for P. ovale wallikeri, P. malariae, and P. falciparum directly from blood samples taken from natural infections. Using PacBio Ultra-Low-Input HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C chromatin conformation capture, we overcome limitations posed by low parasite biomass and the absence of in vitro culture for P. ovale wallikeri and P. malariae. These high quality reference genomes resolve previously inaccessible subtelomeric regions that include expanded gene families likely involved in host-parasite interactions, and they enhance our understanding of parasite persistence, transmission, immune evasion and comparative evolutionary studies. This work provides a critical foundation for including these neglected species in global malaria elimination efforts.

42961946.titulo: Challenges and opportunities for strengthening South American responses to insecticide resistance in disease vectors: Lessons from the WINSA workshop in Bogotá, Colombia.
42961946.autores: Martins AJ, Ahumada M, … Corbel V (21 autores)
42961946.resumo:
Vector-borne diseases remain a major and evolving public health challenge in South America, where arboviruses such as dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and malaria continue to expand in incidence and geographic distribution. Insecticides remain central to vector control programs; however, the rapid emergence and spread of insecticide resistance across multiple vector species increasingly threaten the effectiveness and sustainability of these interventions. In response to these challenges, the Worldwide Insecticide Resistance Network-South America (WINSA) organized a regional workshop in Bogotá, Colombia, in March 2026 to assess the current status of insecticide resistance, identify research priorities, and strengthen regional collaboration.
The workshop brought together experts from 13 South American countries and territories representing academia, public health institutions, and international organizations. Sixteen presentations addressed the current status of insecticide resistance in major disease vectors, including mosquitoes and triatomines. Discussions covered surveillance systems, resistance mechanisms, molecular and genomic tools, operational challenges, and innovative vector control strategies.
The workshop highlighted widespread resistance to pyrethroids and organophosphates across multiple vector species in South America. High frequencies of knockdown resistance mutations (kdr) and evidence of metabolic resistance mechanisms were reported in several countries, particularly in the dengue vector Aedes aegypti. Emerging resistance to novel insecticide formulations was also identified. Participants emphasized major disparities in surveillance capacity, insufficient standardization of methodologies, and uneven geographical coverage across the region. An Integrated Vector Resistance management framework, integrating biological, molecular, genomic, and spatial surveillance approaches, was proposed to support evidence-based decision-making in vector control. Innovative approaches, including insecticide combinations, spatial repellents, and insecticidal paints, were presented as promising complementary tools for integrated vector management.
Insecticide resistance represents a growing threat to the control of arboviral and malaria vectors in South America. Strengthening harmonized surveillance systems, integrating molecular and genomic tools, and improving regional coordination are critical priorities. WINSA provides a strategic scientific and technical platform to support collaborative research, capacity building, harmonized resistance surveillance, and the translation of resistance evidence into information that can support vector-control decision-making across the region.

42961863.titulo: Antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cytotoxicity and larvicidal activities of Ziziphus oenopolia leaves: in vitro and in silico studies.
42961863.autores: Ramalingam SV, Soloman VG, … Lo YH (9 autores)
42961863.resumo: The present study investigated the phytochemical composition, in vitro and in silico biological activities, and insecticidal properties of Ziziphus oenopolia (L) Mill. leaf extracts. The LC-MS profile of Ziziphus oenopolia leaves extract, which identified major phytochemical classes of fatty acids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids. The GC-MS profile, including n-hexadecanoic acid, phytol, and 9,12,15-octadecatrienoic acid, which were predicted by PASS and ADMET profiling to exhibit strong antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, cytotoxic, and larvicidal activities. The hydroalcoholic extract demonstrated the highest biological efficacy across multiple assays. In vitro antioxidant evaluation revealed strong DPPH and ABTS radical scavenging activities with IC₅₀ values of 41.04 and 43.54 µg/mL, respectively. The extract also showed significant protein anti-denaturation effects against bovine serum albumin and egg albumin (IC₅₀ = 315.53 and 311.60 µg/mL), significant cytotoxicity (EC₅₀ = 173.92 µg/mL), and strong larvicidal activity (LC₅₀ = 126.09 µg/mL for Aedes aegypti and 136.01 µg/mL for Tribolium castaneum), all exhibiting dose-dependent inhibition. In silico molecular docking further supported these findings, revealing strong binding affinities of the phytoconstituents toward human peroxiredoxin 5 as an antioxidant target, COX-2 (PDB: 1PXX) as an anti-inflammatory target, EGFR (PDB: 2EB3) as an anticancer target, and juvenile hormone binding protein (PDB: 5V13) as a larvicidal target. Overall, Z. oenopolia may contribute to the development of natural antioxidants and anti-inflammatory agents for mitigating oxidative stress-related and chronic inflammatory diseases.

42961025.titulo: Oya virus reporter systems for high-throughput screening of viral replication inhibitors in mosquito cells.
42961025.autores: Chen W, Xiong G, … Xia H (12 autores)
42961025.resumo: Orthobunyaviruses are a diverse group of arboviruses, yet reporter virus-based inhibitor screening in mosquito-derived cells remains underexplored. Oya virus (OYAV), a Simbu serogroup orthobunyavirus detected in humans, mosquitoes, and midges, currently lacks reverse genetics tools and quantitative compound screening platforms. In this study, we established the first plasmid-based reverse genetics system for OYAV, successfully rescuing recombinant wild-type virus (rOYAV/WT) alongside fluorescent reporter viruses expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (rOYAV/eGFP/S) or mCherry (rOYAV/mCherry/S). Both reporter viruses maintained stable reporter expression and infectivity across multiple vertebrate and mosquito-derived cell lines, although reporter insertion resulted in attenuated replication compared with the parental virus. Leveraging the robust fluorescence signal and retention of the reporter-containing region during serial passage, we developed a mosquito cell-based high-content screening platform to identify compounds inhibiting OYAV replication in C6/36 cells. The assay demonstrated high robustness and reproducibility, with a Z' factor of 0.755, and showed strong correlation with wild-type virus replication profiles. By screening an 800-compound library, we identified 10 candidates exhibiting >95% inhibitory activity against OYAV replication. Among these, saikosaponin B2, fingolimod (hydrochloride), and fangchinoline displayed micromolar inhibitory effects against both reporter and wild-type OYAV replication, with limited cytotoxicity in C6/36 cells. Collectively, this study establishes the reverse genetics system for OYAV and a quantitative mosquito-cell-based screening platform for orthobunyavirus replication inhibitors, providing a valuable tool for studying OYAV replication and evaluating antiviral compounds in mosquito-derived cells.IMPORTANCEOya virus (OYAV) is an emerging arbovirus circulating in Asia, with documented infection in humans and arthropod vectors. However, the absence of reverse genetics and reporter systems has limited mechanistic studies and inhibitor discovery for OYAV, particularly in arthropod-derived cells. Here, we established a reverse genetics system and generated fluorescent reporter viruses that enable real-time monitoring of OYAV replication. The optimized reporter virus was further used to establish a high-throughput inhibitor screening platform in mosquito C6/36 cells, leading to the identification of three compounds with inhibitory activity and low cytotoxicity in this system. These tools provide a foundation for investigating OYAV biology and facilitate the discovery and evaluation of inhibitors in vector cells and potentially in live vectors.

42956101.titulo: Leptospirosis occurs as frequently as malaria among adolescent and adult acute febrile patients in Hoima, Uganda: A prospective health facility-based study.
42956101.autores: Kirabo AV, Alinaitwe L, … Dreyfus A (12 autores)
42956101.resumo:
Leptospirosis is underdiagnosed across sub-Saharan Africa, with its contribution to acute undifferentiated fever (AUF) poorly characterized. We determined the prevalence, risk factors, and clinical profile of leptospirosis among adolescents and adults with AUF at a referral hospital and health centre in Hoima, Uganda.
In a prospective health facility-based study with convalescent follow-up, blood and urine from AUF patients were tested by LipL32 real-time PCR (qPCR) and microscopic agglutination (MAT). Leptospirosis was confirmed by qPCR positivity, a single test MAT titre of ≥1:800, a fourfold titre rise or seroconversion (change from negative or 1:50 to ≥1:100 (lenient) or ≥1:200 (conservative)) in paired sera. Risk factors were identified by multivariable logistic regression.
Among 330 AUF patients, acute leptospirosis prevalence was 27.0% under the conservative definition (95% CI 22.3 to 32.1) and 32.7% under the lenient definition (95% CI 27.7 to 38.1). This was comparable to malaria at 30.3% (95% CI 25.3 to 35.3), and 8.8% of patients had both infections (95% CI 5.7 to 11.8). qPCR detected Leptospira DNA in 9.1% of patients. Agreement between qPCR and serology was low: 63.3% of qPCR-positive cases were confirmed by MAT, and only 24.4% of serologically confirmed cases were qPCR-positive. Seroprevalence (MAT titre 1:100 or above) was 35.8% (95% CI 30.6 to 41.2). L. interrogans serovar Bataviae was the predominant serovar, reported here for the first time in Uganda. Skinning animals (aOR 5.19, 95% CI 1.40 to 21.16) and mosquito exposure (aOR 2.31, 95% CI 1.17 to 4.70) were independent risk factors.
Leptospirosis occurs as frequently as malaria among AUF patients in Hoima warranting inclusion in Uganda's national febrile illness guidelines. The association of leptospirosis with skinning suggests a role of animal exposure in leptospirosis transmission. Poor qPCR-MAT concordance confirms that accurate case ascertainment requires combined molecular and serological diagnostics. While findings are regional, their implications are broader, highlighting the need to include zoonotic diseases in diagnosis and surveillance. Targeted treatment can reduce morbidity, mortality, and economic burden, while limiting antimicrobial resistance by decreasing broad-spectrum antibiotic use.

42956080.titulo: Type III CI factors from wAlbB induce cytoplasmic incompatibility via a Host Modification mechanism.
42956080.autores: Hou X, Goh FG, … Cai Y (7 autores)
42956080.resumo: The widespread prevalence of the endosymbiotic bacterium Wolbachia among insect species relies on its ability to invade and manipulate host reproduction via several ways, among which cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI) is most studied. Two non-mutually exclusive models, the Host-Modification (HM) and the Toxin-Antidote (TA), have been proposed to explain the molecular basis of CI. Here, we investigate the CI-inducing activity of the Type III CI factors (cifs) from wAlbB, a strain currently being deployed to combat mosquito-borne diseases. This set of Cifs displays conserved subcellular localization dynamics in various insect cells. Both cifA and cifB are required for the induction of DNA damage in cultured cells, and transgenic Drosophila. Moreover, these cifs induce CI in Drosophila through the two-by-one manner, meaning cifA and cifB act together during spermatogenesis to induce CI, and maternal cifA can reverse the effect. Mechanistically, genetic, biochemical, cellular, and proteomic analyses reveal that this pair of cifs acts during the early stage of spermatogenesis but is dispensable in late-stage germline cells for CI induction. Collectively, our findings support the notion that wAlbB Type III cifs induce CI via a HM-based mechanism. Additional analyses suggest that different Wolbachia strains may employ distinct molecular mechanisms to induce CI.

42955857.titulo: Natural Occurrence and Molecular Diversity of Wolbachia Endosymbiont DNA in Wild Mosquito Populations of Central India.
42955857.autores: Khan N, Jain M, … Das A (4 autores)
42955857.revista: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
42955857.resumo:
Utilizing Wolbachia for mosquito biocontrol requires baseline understanding of natural infection dynamics, lineage diversity, and host-symbiont phylogenetic concordance across native vector populations.
We collected 2,167 adult mosquitoes (Anopheles, Culex, Aedes, and Mansonia) across five districts in central India (Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh). Specimens were screened in 263 genus-level pools via wsp PCR. Positive pools were brought to individuals level, typed across three different loci (ftsZ, gltA, and GroEL) of Wolbachia spp., and validated by mosquito barcoding (cox1, ITS2). Maximum likelihood phylogenies were constructed for all six loci both for Wolbachia (four) and mosquitoes (two).
Overall, 27 pools (10.26%) and 49 individuals (21.21%) were wsp-positive that includes 17 Anopheles, 18 Culex, 9 Aedes, and 5 Mansonia. Culicines exhibited robust multilocus amplification, whereas all 17 Anopheles failed to amplify at ftsZ, gltA, and GroEL. Phylogenetic trees of the mosquito-host cox1 and ITS2 resolved all four genera and five wsp-positive Anopheles species into monophyletic clades with 84-100% bootstrap support. In Wolbachia phylogenies, culicine isolates clustered in Supergroup B (wPip), with ftsZ and gltA trees resolving Mansonia symbionts into a well-supported, distinct lineage (95-97% bootstrap). Crucially, the wsp tree revealed that four An. annularis sequences formed a monophyletic clade (89-98% bootstrap), clustering with the bat-fly endosymbiont Penicillidia jenynsii rather than mosquito-adapted strains. Primary malaria vectors (An. culicifacies and An. fluviatilis) tested negative for Wolbachia.
Phylogenetic divergence and housekeeping gene dropout indicate that wsp detection in wild Anopheles represents transient or horizontal acquisition rather than stable intracellular endosymbiosis. Multilocus phylogenetic validation is critical prior to deploying symbiont-based biocontrol.

42955847.titulo: Larvicidal activity of Zanthoxylum oxyphyllum Edgew. extract against Culex pipiens.
42955847.autores: Zoramthara K, Manngaihsiam R, … Kharat KR (8 autores)
42955847.revista: Journal of environmental science and health. Part. B, Pesticides, food contaminants, and agricultural wastes
42955847.resumo: The increasing incidence of synthetic pesticide resistance in Culex pipiens, a principal vector for lymphatic filariasis, demands the immediate advancement of sustainable mosquitocides. This current research shows the larvicidal effectiveness, molecular processes, and environmental safety of the plant extract Zanthoxylum oxyphyllum (ZOM). Metabolite profiling using Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) showed the presence of flavonoid glycosides such as fortunellin and linarin, phenolic derivatives, and nitrogenous metabolites. ZOM showed larvicidal action against day-2 third-instar C. pipiens that depended on the dose and the period. The LC50 and LC90 values decreased from 43.14 (30.78-60.45) ppm and 132.46 (94.52-185.65) ppm at 12 h to 36.16 (26.06-50.16) ppm and 99.163 (71.48-137.56) ppm at 24 h, which showed that the activity of the treatment increased with time. Compared to untreated controls, ZOM-treated larvae had lower levels of both alkaline phosphatase (0.03797 vs. 0.00282 U mg-1 protein) and acetylcholinesterase (0.00396 vs. 0.00153 U mg-1 protein) activity. Standardized acute toxicity testing, as per OECD 2025 recommendations, aids in showing that ZOM does not harm the non-target indicator species Danio rerio. These results may confirm that ZOM is an effective, target-specific, and environmentally acceptable option for sustainable vector control programs against mosquitoes.

42952207.titulo: Abundance and species diversity of mosquitoes (Diptera, Culicidae) in endemic areas for arboviruses in the Eastern Amazon, Brazil.
42952207.autores: David EDS, Komninakis SV, … Souto RNP (7 autores)
42952207.resumo: Combating the spread of arboviruses in the Amazon relies on understanding the diversity of Culicidae, particularly potential vectors. Areas with historical records of vector occurrence provide crucial insights into the factors driving epidemic emergence. Furthermore, anthropogenic activities, such as deforestation and demographic pressure on the forest, are considered the primary drivers of new outbreaks, creating a scenario of high ecological receptivity for pathogens of public health concern. This study aimed to estimate mosquito richness and abundance in arbovirus-endemic areas within the districts of Carvão and Mazagão Velho, in the municipality of Mazagão, Amapá, Eastern Amazon. Four Culicidae sampling sites were established in each locality, utilizing CDC light traps and Human Landing Catch (HLC). Sampling campaigns began in January 2024 and concluded in December 2024, spanning both the rainy and less rainy seasons of the Amazon region. Specimens were identified at the Arthropoda Laboratory of the Federal University of Amapá. This research documented a total of 3.671 adult mosquitoes from the Culicidae family, encompassing 35 different species across 11 distinct genera. Only four genera are not considered arbovirus vectors in humans. The remaining genera include species of medical and epidemiological importance in arbovirus transmission, including species from the genera Anopheles, Aedes, Psorophora, Haemagogus, Culex, Coquillettidia and Mansonia. Environmental conditions favour high ecological receptivity for potential vectors, indicating a need for entomological surveillance near the study areas. Understanding the diversity of Culicidae reveals the importance of vector control in combating mosquito-borne pathogens in the Amazon.

42959520.titulo: Assessing dengue vector breeding in diverse environments for targeted interventions: Case studies from Colombia and Nepal.
42959520.autores: Barahona E, Nelson-Cofie D, … Banjara MR (6 autores)
42959520.revista: Current research in parasitology & vector-borne diseases
42959520.resumo: Dengue and other Aedes-borne diseases are increasing globally, with vector control being the primary prevention strategy in the absence of an effective vaccine. Because mosquitoes breed in domestic water containers, identifying the most productive container types is essential for targeted interventions. This study compared pupal productivity of Aedes spp. and productive container types in two settings in Colombia and Nepal with distinct environmental, epidemiological, and water storage characteristics. A pupal/demographic survey was conducted in Valledupar, Colombia, and Triyuga Municipality, Nepal, including 300 and 121 households, respectively. Pupal counts were used as a proxy for adult mosquito production. In Colombia, 16 of 506 containers were productive, with large water storage containers accounting for over 90% of pupae. In Nepal, 34 of 396 containers were productive, with containers such as barrels and flower vases contributing most pupae. In both locations, pupal production was highly clustered in a small number of containers. These findings show that the most productive breeding sites differ between places, with large containers dominating in Colombia and smaller containers in Nepal. Targeted vector control strategies should therefore, focus on the specific container types responsible for most pupal production in each context. Context-specific interventions guided by pupal/demographic surveys are essential for efficient dengue control.

42952897.titulo: Household environmental management practices, community engagement, and self-reported malaria incidence in urban and rural communities of Malawi.
42952897.resumo: Malaria control in Malawi relies primarily on long-lasting insecticide-treated nets (LLITNs) and indoor residual spraying (IRS), but transmission remains heterogeneous across districts. Previous research indicates that community-based environmental management strategies, such as routine drainage maintenance, vegetation removal, and effective household waste disposal, may reduce environmental conditions conducive to malaria vector proliferation. This study investigated the association between environmental management practices at both household and community levels and self-reported cases of malaria in Malawi. We disseminated an online survey through social media from December 2024 to February 2025, targeting adults in both rural and urban locales, resulting in 282 participants. Negative binomial regression was employed to assess the relationship between preventive measures, household-level environmental management practices, community engagement, and malaria cases during the past year. LLITNs were the most used preventive measure (62.1%). Their use was significantly associated with fewer malaria cases in rural areas (p = 0.035) but more malaria cases in urban areas (p = 0.018). Household-level (94.3%) and community-level (70.9%) environmental management practices were widely reported but showed weak and area-dependent associations with malaria incidence. Regardless of area of residence, respondents faced difficulties maintaining these practices, mostly due to time constraints (49.3%) and financial constraints (61.3%). Strengthening community education, resource support, and integration of environmental management into existing programs is likely to be needed to sustain these practices. The contrasting rural-urban patterns may reflect unmeasured differences in local transmission intensity and warrant investigation in studies with geographically resolved data.

42960467.titulo: Identification of Usutu virus in blood donors as part of molecular screening for West Nile virus, France, 2023.
42960467.autores: Gallian P, Grard G, … de Lamballerie X (20 autores)
42960467.revista: Euro surveillance : bulletin Europeen sur les maladies transmissibles = European communicable disease bulletin
42960467.resumo: BACKGROUNDWest Nile Virus (WNV) can be transmitted via blood transfusion and lead to neuroinvasive forms in recipients of blood products.AIMWe aimed to investigate WNV and Usutu virus (USUV) infections among blood donors in France.METHODSBlood donations in 18 of 96 departments of metropolitan France and from travellers returning from affected areas were screened prospectively for WNV using a commercial nucleic acid test (NAT). In addition, stored samples from blood donations in the affected departments were retrospectively tested with RT-qPCR. Differentiation between WNV and USUV infections in NAT-positive samples was done with a RT-qPCR or by seroneutralisation after seroconversion.RESULTSBetween 18 July and 1 December 2023, 34 (0.018%) of 185,965 blood donation samples were initially positive for WNV. After investigations, 20 donors with USUV infections (16 confirmed, four probable) and five with WNV infections (three confirmed, two probable) were identified. In samples from four donors, WNV and USUV could not be differentiated, and five samples remained indeterminate. Seventeen USUV infections were considered autochthonous: nine departments in the southern and central parts of France, including two departments where WNV was also detected. Infections with USUV were detected between 21 July and 17 October and WNV between 23 August and 20 September.CONCLUSIONVia screening of blood donations, we could identify the circulation of USUV in 2023 in large parts of metropolitan France. A One Health approach is required to better understand the determinants of USUV circulation in France and the clinical consequences of USUV infections in humans.

42958945.titulo: Malaria and associated factors after RTS,S/AS01 vaccination in children in Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abrem Municipality, Ghana: A facility-based cross-sectional study.
42958945.autores: Aninagyei E, Boatey CA, … Zilevu G (7 autores)
42958945.revista: The Journal of international medical research
42958945.resumo: ObjectiveMalaria remains a major public health challenge in Ghana despite the implementation of multiple control measures, including the RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) malaria vaccine. This study assessed malaria rapid diagnostic test positivity and associated factors among individuals presenting with suspected malaria in the Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abrem District, Ghana.MethodsThis facility-based cross-sectional study included 400 individuals of all age groups who presented with suspected malaria at the Salvation Army Hospital, Ajumako Ba. Malaria was diagnosed using rapid diagnostic tests. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, malaria control practices, environmental exposures, and vaccination status were collected using structured questionnaires. Associations were assessed using chi-square tests and binary logistic regression to identify independent predictors of malaria infection.ResultsThe overall malaria rapid diagnostic test positivity rate was 20.8% (83/400). Malaria test positivity differed significantly by age (p < 0.001), with the highest burden observed among children and adolescents. Sleeping under a mosquito net the preceding night was strongly protective (adjusted odds ratio = 0.17, 95% confidence interval: 0.07-0.40, p < 0.001). In contrast, sharing mosquito nets with one person (adjusted odds ratio = 4.51, 95% confidence interval: 1.31-15.50, p = 0.02), with more than one person (adjusted odds ratio = 4.76, 95% confidence interval: 0.92-24.47, p = 0.06), prolonged nocturnal outdoor activity (adjusted odds ratio = 4.49, 95% confidence interval: 1.44-14.03, p = 0.01), and proximity to gullies or stagnant water (adjusted odds ratio = 2.49, 95% confidence interval: 1.24-5.01, p = 0.01) significantly increased malaria risk. Among children younger than 7 years, malaria prevalence was lower in RTS,S/AS01-vaccinated children (29.6%) compared to unvaccinated children (60%), although differences were not statistically significant overall. Significant associations in this age group were observed with mosquito net use, nocturnal outdoor activity, and nearby vegetation.ConclusionMalaria rapid diagnostic test positivity remains high in the Komenda-Edina-Eguafo-Abrem Municipality, particularly among children. Mosquito net use, nocturnal outdoor activity, and proximity to potential mosquito breeding sites were associated with rapid diagnostic test positivity. The small vaccine-eligible subgroup limited conclusions on RTS,S/AS01 vaccination. Integrated, community-based malaria control strategies remain essential for sustained reductions in malaria transmission.

42960654.titulo: Preliminary case study of vertical distribution and trap efficiency of Aedes (Diptera: Culicidae) mosquitoes in urban multi-storey buildings in Selangor, Malaysia.
42960654.autores: Zurkarnain MA, Rahman MA, … Agustar HK (7 autores)
42960654.resumo: The increasing prevalence of high-rise residential developments in dengue-endemic regions has created new challenges for understanding the distribution and surveillance of Aedes mosquitoes. This study investigated the vertical distribution of Aedes mosquitoes and evaluated the effectiveness of two modified low-cost sticky trap designs in a high-rise residential complex in Hulu Langat, Selangor, Malaysia. A total of 108 sticky traps comprising small and large trap designs were deployed across multiple floor levels in two residential blocks over four sampling rounds. Adult mosquitoes were identified morphologically, and trap performance was assessed using sticky trap indices and Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) analysis. Aedes aegypti was the dominant species captured throughout the study, particularly in Block A, whereas Ae. albopictus was more frequently detected in Block B. Adult Aedes mosquitoes were recorded from lower parking levels to the highest residential floors, demonstrating extensive vertical distribution within the building environment. Large sticky traps consistently outperformed small traps, recording higher sticky trap indices, greater mosquito captures, and all mixed-species detections. Negative-binomial GEE indicated that floor level and trap size were significant predictors of Ae. aegypti abundance, while binary logistic regression showed that the probability of Ae. aegypti detection also increased with floor level and was substantially higher in large traps. These findings demonstrate that Aedes mosquitoes are capable of occupying a wide vertical range in high-rise residential buildings and highlight the value of low-cost stiky traps as practical surveillance tools. The study provides important ecological insights into urban mosquito distribution and supports the development of scalable surveillance strategies for dengue vector management in increasingly vertical urban landscapes.

42958344.titulo: The hidden malaria: misidentification of Plasmodium malariae and Plasmodium ovale in low-transmission setting targeted for elimination in Ethiopia.
42958344.autores: Getachew H, Wang C, … Yewhalaw D (10 autores)
42958344.resumo:
Quartan malaria caused by Plasmodium malariae (Pm) and tertian Plasmodium ovale (Po) malaria has been largely overlooked in Ethiopia due to their milder clinical symptoms, lower prevalence, and frequently misdiagnosis during routine microscopic. This study estimated the prevalence of Pm and Po infections misdiagnosed as P. vivax (Pv) in selected health facilities in southwestern Ethiopia.
A cross-sectional study was conducted among study participants who were positive for Pv by microscopy or rapid diagnostic test (RDT) and who were attending health facilities within Arjo-Didessa sugarcane plantations and surrounding areas in Oromia, southwestern Ethiopia, between September 2019 and July 2022. Of the 3590 febrile patients attending health facilities, 323 were Pv positive by microscopy or RDT. Among these, 245 Pv-positive samples were re-evaluated using quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Species-specific primers targeting Pv, P. falciparum (Pf), Pm, and Po were used for species confirmation.
From 245 vivax malaria cases, RDT were performed to 162 sub-samples, among them 8.6% (14/162) were negative by RDT. None of the samples tested by RDT and microscopy detected Pm or Po. Of these 245 tested and reported as Pv positive by microscopy, qPCR confirmed that 215 (87.7%, 95% CI 82.98-91.58) were positive for Pv, 9 (3.7%, 95% CI 1.69-6.86) for Pf, 8 (3.3%, 95% CI 1.42-6.33) for Pm, 6 (2.4%, 95% CI 0.90-5.25) were positive for Po, and 7 (2.8%, 95% CI 1.16-5.80) had mixed infections (Pf and Pv).
The findings of this study highlights the need for a strategic shift to integrate Pm and Po into Ethiopia's malaria control and elimination program. Moreover, strengthening the diagnostic capacity should include training of microscopists for accurate Plasmodium species identification and adopting highly sensitive diagnostic tool for all four Plasmodium species in resource-limited settings. This is essential for enhancing malaria control and accelerating progress toward elimination.

42958527.titulo: Cost comparison of community-based vector surveillance using VectorCamTM, an AI-enabled mosquito identification tool, versus routine entomological surveillance in Uganda.
42958527.autores: Rincon Torroella M, Raman S, … Acharya S (11 autores)
42958527.resumo:
National malaria elimination programs depend on timely and reliable vector surveillance data to guide interventions. Current systems rely on analog data collection and microscopy-based morphological identification of mosquitoes by entomologists (vector control officers, VCO), a process constrained by limited entomologists, high specimen volumes, and specimen transport from rural collection sites. VectorCamTM is a smartphone-based device that uses AI to classify mosquito species, sex, and abdominal status within seconds, enabling automated workflows and the task-shifting of some entomologist responsibilities to community health workers (CHWs) or village health teams (VHTs). This study evaluated the unit cost of integrating VectorCamTM into routine surveillance in Uganda.
Data were extracted from a 12-month pragmatic parallel randomized trial conducted across two districts in Uganda from 2023 to 2024. This analysis accounted only for costs directly associated with field activities, including personnel, transport, and supplies. Three VectorCamTM implementation models were analyzed. Implementation Model 1 represented full task-shifting of mosquito surveillance responsibilities to village health teams, where they were collected, analyzed, mosquito identified and reported data without the involvement of VCO and the use of VectorCamTM. Implementation Model 2 incorporated quarterly supervision by VCO to support village health team-led activities. Implementation Model 3 included monthly VCO supervision, aligning with routine surveillance workflows, to assess the cost implications of adding digital surveillance to existing protocols.
The annual cost of routine surveillance (control arm) per district was USD $10,615. In comparison, VectorCamTM reduced costs to USD $8,852 in Model 1 (16.6% savings), USD $9,200 in Model 2 (13.3 savings), and USD $9896 in Model 3 (6.8% savings). These reductions were driven primarily by reductions in personnel and transport expenditures, although they were partially offset by higher supply costs associated with devices and service fees. The per-device analysis demonstrated that each VectorCamTM unit represented an annual cost of USD 144.51 but replaced USD 438.29 worth of surveillance functions, resulting in net savings of USD 293.78 per device under Implementation Model 1. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated increased savings in scenarios with existing digital infrastructure or the individual usage of VectorCamTM by one VHT.
Digitalizing vector surveillance with VectorCamTM offers a cost-saving and scalable approach for low- and middle-income countries. By shifting resources from specialized, labor-intensive methods such as microscopy to technology operable by CHW. VectorCamTM supports more efficient data collection while reducing costs. These findings suggest that integrating digital task-shifting tools into national malaria surveillance programs can enhance vector surveillance in resource-constrained settings.

42958273.titulo: Anopheles larval ecology and physicochemical characterization of larval habitats in Dire Dawa: an area colonized by Anopheles stephensi in Eastern Ethiopia.
42958273.autores: Abiy E, Degefa T, … Yewhalaw D (11 autores)
42958273.resumo:
Understanding mosquito larval ecology is crucial for effective vector control strategies. While much is known about Anopheles larval habitat distribution, the impact of landscape (urban vs. rural) on Anopheles stephensi larval distribution and population dynamics in Ethiopia remains unclear.
A longitudinal study was conducted from February 2023 to December 2024 in aquatic habitats in urban, peri-urban, and rural areas of Dire Dawa City Administration, eastern Ethiopia. Mosquito larvae and pupae were collected and reared in a field insectary until adult emergence. The female Anopheles were morphologically identified and further confirmed via polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The physicochemical parameters of the larval habitats were measured via a HANNA multiparameter water probe. Statistical analyses included general linear models, ANOVA, logistic regression, paired sample t tests, chi-square tests, principal component analysis and correlation analyses to assess larval presence, density, and distribution in relation to water physicochemical parameters across the three ecological settings.
A total of 23,526 larvae and 1808 pupae of Anopheles mosquitoes were collected from 856 man-made habitats (bricks, plastic sheets, steel drums, tire tracks, canal ditches, and barrels) and 53 natural habitats (river edges, animal hoof prints, ponds, and swamps) in urban, peri-urban, and rural areas. Uncovered cemented cisterns were the main human-made larval habitats; river edges were the main natural habitats. Anopheles larvae were absent in the steel drums and plastic barrels at the rural sites. Anopheles larval density significantly differed across the different ecological settings (F = 7.8, df = 1, 908, p = 0.005) and among the different larval habitat types (F = 326.2, df = 1, 907, p < 0.001). Among the 2934 reared adults, 74.8% (2194/2934) were An. stephensi, 21.7% (636/2934) were An. arabiensis, and 3.0% were other species (An. pharoensis, An. coustani, An. amharicus, An. pretoriensis). An. stephensi shares habitats with An. arabiensis and An. amharicus. Larval presence was significantly associated with brick factory proximity (χ2 = 23.8, df = 5, p < 0.001), land use/surrounding environment (χ2 = 32.6, df = 13, p = 0.002), vegetation (χ2 = 27.1, df = 12, p = 0.008), shade coverage (χ2 = 25.9, df = 15, p = 0.039), substrate type (χ2 = 34.1, df = 6, p < 0.001), and competitor/predator presence (χ2 = 14.6, df = 1, p = 0.001). However, larval presence was not associated with the presence of larval interventions (χ2 = 1.3, df = 1, p = 0.250). Water pH (r = 0.26, n = 102, p < 0.050) and water pressure (r = 0.21, n = 102, p < 0.050) were the only water physicochemical parameters that were positively correlated with An. stephensi presence.
Anopheles stephensi was dominant in urban areas but was also present in rural areas. Existing larval source management methods do not prevent Anopheles from occurring in many habitats, indicating an urgent need for improved strategies.

42958220.titulo: West Nile virus in Portugal: insights from equine serology.
42958220.autores: Maroco D, Ramos F, … Barros SC (7 autores)
42958220.resumo:
West Nile virus (WNV) is a zoonotic mosquito-borne flavivirus belonging to the family Flaviviridae and the genus Orthoflavivirus. It is primarily transmitted by Culex spp. mosquitoes and maintained in an enzootic cycle involving avian hosts. Humans and horses are considered incidental or dead-end hosts, as they do not sustain onward transmission due to their low viremia levels, although infections may progress to severe neurological disease and death. In Portugal, WNV has circulated in horses almost annually since its first detection in 2004, suggesting endemic establishment.
This study provides updated data on the geographical distribution and annual occurrence of WNV infection in clinically affected horses in mainland Portugal between 2022 and 2025, thereby contributing to a broader understanding of WNV dynamics in southern Europe. As viremia is typically low and short-lived in horses, diagnosis relies primarily on serological methods, particularly the detection of IgM antibodies. IgM analyses identified WNV-seropositive horses in all four years, with 3/9 cases (33.3%) testing positive in 2022, 15/30 (50.0%) in 2023, 32/52 (61.5%) in 2024, and 13/38 (34.2%) in 2025. No WNV RNA was detected in serum samples. Based on clinical signs together with serological results, WNV was diagnosed in 63 of the 129 horses presenting neurological signs.
These findings reinforce the continued circulation of WNV in Portugal and highlight the importance of sustained surveillance in equine populations.

42956783.titulo: Novel dengue serotype 4 live virus human challenge: a phase 1 dose optimisation and homologous rechallenge study.
42956783.autores: Chua JV, Price A, … Lyke KE (15 autores)
42956783.resumo:
Dengue live virus human challenges (LVHCs) are key in dengue vaccine and pharmacological development, to down-select candidates and provide a useful platform for understanding viral-host immunology in a controlled setting. The primary aim of this study was to assess the safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity of a newly derived underattenuated dengue virus serotype-4-LVHC (DENV-4-LVHC) strain intended for future dengue challenge studies.
We conducted a first-in-human, phase 1, non-randomised, open-label study that evaluated the safety and optimised dose of the DENV-4-LVHC strain H-241 in flavivirus-naive healthy adult volunteers. The trial was conducted between April 28, 2022, and Dec 18, 2023, at the University of Maryland (Baltimore, MD, USA) and included a dose-optimisation study in which participants were enrolled into staggered-start, dose-ranging cohorts, beginning with the lowest dose, and homologous rechallenge substudy in which willing, primary-infected participants were rechallenged with the optimised dose of DENV-4 at least 12 months from the primary challenge. Successful challenge was defined as more than 90% participants developing self-limiting mild-to-moderate dengue symptoms with detectable RNAemia. Participants were analysed on the basis of the treatment group (primary infection vs rechallenge). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT05268302).
14 healthy adult participants were enrolled between March 31, 2022, and June 9, 2022 (dose optimisation), and were challenged with a subcutaneous dose of DENV-4-LVHC on June 12, 2023 (rechallenge). The majority were men (11 [79%] of 14), and almost half were non-White (6 [43%]). The mean participant age was 33·6 years (range 20-48). All 14 participants developed viraemia and symptoms consistent with self-limited, mild-to-moderate dengue at an optimised dose of 95 plaque-forming units (low dose). Six (60%) participants (of the original ten from the 2022 cohort) were rechallenged using the optimised dose 1 year after primary challenge, and none developed detectable dengue. Robust antibody responses, plasmablast expansion, and antiviral gene upregulation were seen during primary infection but not after rechallenge. No severe dengue, need for inpatient observation, or dengue challenge-related serious adverse events were observed.
DENV-4-LVHC was found to be safe and highly predictable for use in future challenge studies, to evaluate vaccine and therapeutic candidates. Immunity from previous DENV-4-LVHC infection conferred protection following homologous rechallenge 1 year after primary exposure.
Military Infectious Disease Research Program; Medical Technology Enterprise Consortium.

42962481.titulo: The conformational landscape of dengue NS2B-NS3 protease is modulated by ligand stereochemistry: An integrated molecular dynamics, Markov state modeling, and explainable AI study.
42962481.autores: Bantun F, Chaturvedi N, … Kumar V (8 autores)
42962481.resumo: The dengue virus NS2B-NS3 protease is a validated antiviral target whose pronounced conformational plasticity presents a major challenge for structure-based inhibitor design. Although stereochemistry is a fundamental determinant of molecular recognition, how ligand chirality modulates the dynamic and kinetic states of the protease remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether stereochemical optimization can reshape the conformational landscape of NS2B-NS3 using a series of diketopiperazine (DKPZ)-based ligands and their D-enantiomeric derivatives. An integrated computational framework combining molecular docking, 200-ns molecular dynamics simulations, Markov state modeling (MSM), principal component analysis (PCA), free-energy landscape (FEL) mapping, dynamic residue network (DRN) analysis, MM/PBSA, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) was employed to resolve ligand-induced changes across structural, energetic, kinetic, and communication levels. While all ligands maintained stable engagement with the protease binding pocket, D-enantiomeric derivatives produced markedly distinct conformational signatures. In particular, d-DKPZ promoted compact, energetically favorable conformational ensembles and persistent metastable states, accompanied by reduced flexibility and more organized residue-to-residue communication. MSM further revealed that stereochemical optimization altered state populations and transition dynamics, favoring kinetically persistent conformations rather than highly fluctuating ensembles. DRN and SHAP-based XAI independently converged on key catalytic-pocket and stabilizing residues, providing an interpretable link between ligand stereochemistry, local interactions, and global conformational behavior. Comparative analysis of the parent compounds and their D-enantiomeric analogues reveal how stereochemical changes influence binding energetics, conformational dynamics, and residue communication in dengue NS2B-NS3 protease. These findings establish stereochemical optimization as a promising strategy for guiding the design and prioritization of candidate dengue protease inhibitors.

42963406.titulo: Climate change threatens malaria elimination in the Asia Pacific.
42963406.autores: Fornace K, Hein PS, … Mukhtar M (26 autores)
42963406.resumo: Climate change threatens decades of progress toward malaria elimination across the Asia Pacific. In recent years, reported cases have increased sharply in several regions, including Pakistan following the 2022 floods. However, current research and adaptation strategies have largely focused on gradual warming and shifting transmission seasons and may not fully capture acute operational disruptions in endemic settings. Here we examine how climate change influences malaria through cascading disruptions to health systems, population displacement and ecological change. As a multidisciplinary group of policymakers and researchers, we identify priority actions: integrating malaria control into disaster response, deploying adaptive vector control for displaced populations, strengthening cross-border data sharing, linking early warnings to anticipatory action, and incorporating land-use data into surveillance. Leveraging existing advances in climate policy, digital surveillance and community engagement will be critical. Sustaining elimination will require complementing long-term projections with preparedness for near-term system shocks.

42961129.titulo: Potent reaction hijacking inhibitors of Plasmodium falciparum asparagine tRNA synthetase.
42961129.autores: Ye X, Esherick LY, … Xie SC (32 autores)
42961129.resumo:
Malaria remains one of the major threats to human health. Breakthrough drugs with high potency and low resistance risk are needed to combat the ever-increasing resistance to currently deployed antimalarials. Here, we explore a series of 4-aminoquinazoline-based sulfonamides (4AQS), with a synthetically accessible scaffold. Exemplars exhibit nanomolar potency against blood stage Plasmodium cultures, with up to 300-fold selectivity compared with a mammalian cell line. The compounds are active against transmissible stages of Plasmodium falciparum and refractory to resistance development. Targeted mass spectrometry reveals that the 4AQS compounds act as reaction hijacking inhibitors targeting P. falciparum aminoacyl tRNA synthetases (aaRSs). Subtle changes to the chemical structure switch the main target from cytoplasmic threonine tRNA synthetase (PfThrRS) to cytoplasmic asparagine tRNA synthetase (PfAsnRS), a change that is associated with increased potency against P. falciparum. The target preference was confirmed by selective knockdown of different P. falciparum aaRSs and by tolerance selection in a mutator line. Consistent with aaRS targets, exemplar compounds activate the amino acid starvation response. Recombinant enzyme inhibition and thermal stabilization assays confirm the susceptibility of PfAsnRS to reaction hijacking and show that human AsnRS is less susceptible. A molecular model of Asn-tRNA-bound PfAsnRS reveals that a potent hijacker adopts a pose similar to adenosine 5'-monophosphate (AMP). An AlphaFold model of the native PfAsnRS dimer helps explain the tolerance-conferring effect of a mutation at the dimer interface.
Every year, at least 200 million new malaria infections are diagnosed, causing more than 600,000 deaths in Africa and Southeast Asia. Ever-increasing levels of resistance to current antimalarials are leading to an impending crisis. Breakthrough drugs with new modes of action are much needed. Here, we explore a series of inhibitors that hijack critical malaria parasite enzymes. The target enzymes catalyze the formation of a bond between the hijackers and an enzyme substrate, forming a tight-binding compound that disrupts the malaria parasite's protein translation machinery. The hijacking inhibitors exhibit high-level potency against the disease-causing stage of the malaria parasite and are also active against transmissible stages. They exhibit up to 300-fold selectivity compared with a mammalian cell line, possess drug-like chemical attributes, and are easily synthesized. Importantly, the compounds are refractory to resistance development.

42956399.titulo: Clinical Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax Infections in the Ethiopian Highlands Were Uncommonly Associated with Recent Travel.
42956399.autores: Lown LA, Ewnetu Y, … Koepfli C (6 autores)
42956399.revista: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
42956399.resumo: The Ethiopian highlands were historically believed to be malaria-free, yet clinical cases are frequently observed in health centers at elevations above 2,000 m. The proportion of cases that recently returned from the lowlands where malaria is endemic, seasonal patterns, and risk factors for infection are poorly described. Febrile patients were enrolled from November 2019 to September 2020 in a health center in Gondar, Ethiopia, at an elevation of 2,100 m. Plasmodium falciparum and P. vivax were detected by microscopy conducted at the health center and by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). A total of 183 P. falciparum infections were typed for hrp2 and hrp3 gene deletions (hrp2: 2.7%; hrp3: 55.2%; dual: 21.9%), and 1,819 participants were enrolled. Test positivity by microscopy and qPCR was 58.1% and 64.1% for P. falciparum, and 41.8% and 35.9% for P. vivax; 3.1% of individuals reported travel to the lowlands within 4 weeks prior to sample collection. Travel increased the odds of malaria infection by 4.1 times, but 92.4% of individuals who tested positive did not report travel. Adults 16 to 35 years of age accounted for 57% of individuals who presented for testing, and test positivity peaked in this age group (P. falciparum: 27.3%; P. vivax: 10.9%). Most individuals who were malaria-positive had not traveled, suggesting that local transmission is occurring within the Ethiopian highlands. The concentration of infections in adult males points to a strong behavior-related risk of infection.

42963786.titulo: Spatial surveillance of Plasmodium falciparum Kelch 13 mutations reveals High-Frequency A675V and the First Molecular Evidence of Suspected Partial Artemisinin Resistance in Baringo in Kenya.
42963786.autores: Akala HM, Opot BH, … Ogutu BR (30 autores)
42963786.resumo:
This surveillance study evaluated the polymorphisms of Pfk13 gene in samples from symptomatic individuals from eight geographically distinct locations in Kenya to determine the prevalence of mutations associated with partial artemisinin resistance.
Between 2018 and 2024, blood samples from individuals with symptoms of uncomplicated malaria at eight hospitals in four of the five distinct malaria transmission zones of Kenya were sequenced for single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in Pfk13 and Pfmdr1. Subsequent positive samples were tested to monitor treatment outcomes.
A total of 44/675 (3.0%) samples harbored 49 Pfk13 mutations. These include 14 nonsynonymous mutations at Pfk13: A675V (n =  3.0%) A578S (n = 4, 0.6%), C469Y (n = 3, 0.44%), V386A (n = 1, 0.15%), P553L (n = 1, 0.15%), R561H/P (n = 1, 0.15%), S522C (n = 1, 0.15%), K455E (n = 1, 0.15%), S600F (n = 1, 0.15%), E612D (n = 1, 0.15%), N489K (n = 1, 0.15%), F491L (n = 1, 0.15%) plus A504V (n = 1, 0.15%). Four WHO-validated markers of partial artemisinin resistance were detected in 25/675 (3.7%) samples. Most Pfk13 A675V mutations (n = 12, 1.8%), constituting 60% of all Pfk13 mutations observed by this study were detected in Baringo County, where the mutation frequency reached 12/71 (16.9%), exceeding the WHO 5% threshold for classification of areas with suspected partial artemisinin resistance. This represents the first molecular evidence consistent with suspected artemisinin resistance in Baringo County.   CONCLUSION: The detection of four WHO-validated Pfk13 markers of partial artemisinin resistance across multiple malaria transmission zones indicates emerging artemisinin resistance in Kenya. The high frequency of A675V in Baringo provides the first molecular evidence consistent with suspected partial artemisinin resistance in Kenya and highlights the need for enhanced therapeutic efficacy, deployment of Multiple First-line Therapies, and molecular surveillance.

42959071.titulo: Dehydration in Tropical Fevers: Rethinking Fluid and Electrolyte Replacement.
42959071.autores: Chatterjee N, Gilada T, … Bangale N (6 autores)
42959071.resumo: Tropical fevers, including dengue, malaria, typhoid, chikungunya, leptospirosis, and scrub typhus, impose a substantial and growing public health burden in the tropical and subtropical regions, particularly the Indian subcontinent. Climate change, monsoon season, and inadequate sanitation further exacerbate transmission dynamics and outbreak patterns. Dehydration represents a critical yet frequently underrecognized complication of these infections. It is attributed to high-grade fever, vomiting, excessive sweating, decreased oral intake, and pathophysiological mechanisms, such as plasma leakage in dengue, hemolysis in malaria, and gastrointestinal losses in typhoid. Electrolyte disturbances, specifically hyponatremia, hypokalemia, and hypochloremia, contribute to the severity of these conditions and likelihood of multi-organ failure. Inadequate hydration amplifies underlying physiological dysfunction, including hemoconcentration, hypovolemic shock, acute kidney injury, and cardiovascular compromise, thereby increasing hospitalization rates, morbidity, and mortality. This review explores the disease-specific hydration challenges across diverse tropical fevers and evaluates the current strategies for effective fluid management. The World Health Organization (WHO), United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF), and national guidelines recommend oral rehydration therapy, formulated with optimized sodium and glucose concentrations to promote rehydration through facilitation of the intestinal sodium-glucose co-transporter (SGLT1) mechanism for management of ambulatory and mild-to-moderate cases. Its efficacy in symptom relief, minimizing intravenous fluid requirements, and accelerating clinical recovery is well established. However, individualized and careful calibration of fluid management remains essential to prevent fluid overload and other related complications. Thus, integrating standardized, evidence-based hydration protocols into routine clinical practice holds the potential to be a practical and cost-effective strategy for managing tropical infection in India and other regions with similar climatic and epidemiological settings.

42958349.titulo: High prevalence of pfmdr1 and pfpm2 amplification and pfmdr1 haplotypes in Plasmodium falciparum isolates circulating in Ghana.
42958349.autores: Kassim AR, Younge PA, … Amenga-Etego LN (16 autores)
42958349.resumo:
In Ghana, artemether-lumefantrine (AL), and artesunate-amodiaquine (AS-AQ) are the main first-line ACTs for uncomplicated malaria, with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHA-PPQ) as an alternative treatment regimen. Copy Number Polymorphisms (CNPs) in Plasmodium falciparum multidrug resistance 1 (pfmdr1) and plasmepsin 2 (pfpm2) genes, as well as specific pfmdr1 haplotypes have been implicated in resistance to AL and DHA-PPQ partner drugs.
This study characterised pfmdr1 and pfpm2 CNPs and pfmdr1 haplotypes in 900 clinical malaria samples across three transmission zones in Ghana. Using a SYBR Green-based Quantitative real-time Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR) assay, followed by targeted amplicon sequencing.
Successful pfmdr1 and pfpm2 amplifications were detected in 32.0% (n = 288) and 27.8% (n = 250) isolates respectively. No significant difference in the prevalence of these gene amplifications was observed across the three eco-epidemiological zones (pfmdr1: p = 0.888; pfpm2: p = 0.081). Furthermore, a weak positive correlation was observed between pfmdr1 and pfpm2 copy numbers (ρ = 0.196), suggesting limited co-selection of these loci. Pfmdr1 haplotype analysis at codons N86Y, Y184F, and D1246Y revealed a high prevalence (55.6%) of the NFD haplotype linked to lumefantrine selection. Interestingly, this haplotype allele was equally prevalent among isolates carrying single or multiple gene copy numbers.
Taken together, this study observed increased prevalence of pfmdr1 and pfpm2 gene amplification in Ghana. Also, a high frequency of the single mutant NFD pfmdr1 haplotype suggesting ongoing selection pressure potentially driven by widespread AL use in Ghana. In addition, pfpm2 CNP has been associated with piperaquine resistance. These findings provide a critical baseline for ongoing molecular surveillance as an early warning for ACT partner drug resistance in Ghana.

42958045.titulo: First report of culturable fungi associated with the Brazilian sharpnose shark (Rhizoprionodon lalandii) from southeastern Brazil.
42958045.autores: Oliveira MME, da Costa GL, … Hauser-Davis RA (6 autores)
42958045.resumo:
Climate change and other anthropogenic environmental changes may alter fungal distributions and ecological interactions, potentially facilitating the emergence or redistribution of opportunistic fungi in marine ecosystems. These shifts raise concerns regarding microbial contamination in seafood and the need for surveillance in marine organisms. Elasmobranchs, such as sharks and rays, are ecologically and economically important but remain understudied regarding fungal occurrence in wild populations. This study provides the first report of cultivable fungal taxa associated with the Brazilian sharpnose shark (Rhizoprionodon lalandii) from southeastern Brazil.
Swabs from the mouth, gills, and cloaca were obtained from 22 specimens procured from artisanal fisheries in Cabo Frio, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Fungal occurrence varied among sampled anatomical sites and individuals, with several cloacal samples showing abundant growth under the culture conditions employed. Recovered isolates consisted primarily of members of the Candida parapsilosis species complex and Meyerozyma guilliermondii, alongside occasional detection of other yeast taxa including Rhodotorula mucilaginosa, Debaryomyces hansenii, Trichosporon japonicum, and Pichia terricola. Because fungal recovery relied on culture-based methods, ITS sequencing of representative colonies, and sampling restricted to external and cloacal tissues, the detected assemblage likely reflects predominant culturable taxa rather than total fungal diversity. Furthermore, implications for food safety, transmission pathways, or environmental contamination remain speculative and warrant targeted investigation.
These findings expand current knowledge regarding fungi associated with R. lalandii and highlight the need for additional studies incorporating environmental sampling, edible tissue analyses, and broader fungal characterization approaches to better understand potential ecological and public health implications.

42960458.titulo: Mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives of mucosal glycosylation-innate immunity crosstalk in inflammatory bowel disease (Review).
42960458.autores: Liu X, Zhang T, … Han X (9 autores)
42960458.resumo: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a group of chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract, driven by a complex interplay of genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, intestinal microbiota dysbiosis and immune dysregulation. In recent years, mucosal glycosylation has emerged as a fundamental molecular determinant of intestinal barrier integrity and function and is increasingly recognized as a key regulatory interface linking the microbiota with host immune responses. Concurrently, the innate immune system serves an important role in mucosal defense and inflammatory responses through pattern recognition receptor‑mediated signaling, and its aberrant activation represents a key driver of persistent inflammation in IBD. The present review systematically summarizes the bidirectional regulatory crosstalk between mucosal glycosylation and innate immunity. The mechanistic roles of glycosylation modifications are highlighted in pathogen recognition, inflammatory signal transduction, inflammasome activation and maintenance of mucosal barrier integrity. Conversely, it is discussed how innate immune activation regulates glycan biosynthesis and remodeling through inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress and major signaling pathways, thereby reshaping the mucosal glycome in disease contexts. On this basis, the dynamic alterations of glycosylation‑innate immunity interactions across different stages of IBD, including disease initiation, progression and relapse, are delineated, emphasizing their important role in sustaining chronic inflammation and driving tissue remodeling. In addition, emerging therapeutic strategies targeting glycosylation pathways, glycan‑lectin interactions, mucosal barrier restoration and microbiota modulation are summarized. The potential of glycomics, multi‑omics integration and glyco‑immune biomarkers in disease stratification and precision medicine are also discussed. By integrating perspectives from glycobiology and immunology, the present review aims to provide a conceptual framework and novel directions for mechanistic research and targeted therapy in IBD.

42953735.titulo: Spatiotemporally coordinated immunometabolic-hyperthermia therapy for diabetic bone defect regeneration.
42953735.autores: Wang L, Peng X, … Wang Z (7 autores)
42953735.resumo: Diabetic bone defects (DBDs) are typified by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and microbial infection within the diabetic microenvironment, which collectively hinder osteogenesis and angiogenesis. Herein, we introduce an Immunometabolic-Hyperthermia Therapy (IMHT) strategy based on a dual-functional nanoplatform, namely a polydopamine/itaconate-incorporated agarose/gelatin (PIAG) hydrogel. This system is fabricated by incorporating itaconic acid (ITA) into polydopamine (PDA) nanoparticles through in situ polymerization, followed by encapsulation within a gelatin/agarose matrix. ITA primarily provides immunometabolic regulation, while PDA enables a tunable photothermal response.
