Upon localized photothermal heating (∼50 °C), the PIAG hydrogel effectively disrupts bacterial biofilms, with photothermal treatment providing the dominant antibacterial effect and ITA offering an additional supportive contribution. Upon mild photothermal activation (∼41 °C), IMHT mitigates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, inhibits neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and reprograms macrophages toward an M2-like reparative phenotype through JAK1/STAT1 pathway inhibition. The resulting pro-regenerative immune milieu enhances fibroblast growth factor-2 (FGF-2) secretion, while heat-induced activation of HSP90 stabilizes FGF-2/FGFR1 signaling, further promoting osteogenic differentiation and endothelial migration. Overall, the spatiotemporally coordinated antibacterial, immunometabolic, and regenerative regulation realized by IMHT offers a comprehensive and effective strategy for the repair of diabetic bone defects.

42959445.titulo: Atherosclerosis: From Pathogenesis to Therapeutic Interventions.
42959445.autores: Zhou E, Zhan C, … Jiang L (10 autores)
42959445.resumo: Atherosclerosis is no longer viewed solely as a lipid-storage disorder but rather as a complex multisystem inflammatory disease driven by interactions among the vascular, immune, metabolic, and nervous systems. This review integrates recent concepts, including trained immunity, the neuroimmune cardiovascular interface, vascular cell plasticity, and the microbiome-vascular axis, that reshape the understanding of plaque initiation, progression, and instability. We summarize how established lipid-lowering, antidiabetic, antihypertensive, and revascularization strategies influence atherosclerotic disease and discuss emerging interventions, including RNA therapeutics, anti-inflammatory agents, gene therapy, and cell-based approaches. Key ongoing clinical trials that may clarify the cardiovascular benefits and safety of these strategies are also reviewed. Despite therapeutic advances, residual cardiovascular risk persists because of limitations in animal models, sex-related differences in plaque phenotype, and the lack of clinically applicable biomarkers. Nanotechnology, human microphysiological systems, spatial multiomics, and artificial intelligence may help bridge these translational gaps. Successful clinical implementation will nevertheless require biomarker-guided patient selection, rational combination therapy, validated surrogate endpoints, long-term safety assessment, and attention to health economics. In summary, these advances will shape future translational research and clinical trial design, ultimately advancing personalized management of atherosclerosis.

42962054.titulo: Metabolic licensing of innate immune memory.
42962054.resumo: NAD+ is revealed to be a metabolic signal that preserves an epigenetic mark central to trained immunity by inhibiting the histone demethylase KDM5a (see related Research Article by Jin et al.).

42962052.titulo: Nuclear NAD+ promotes innate immune memory by inhibiting KDM5A-dependent histone demethylation.
42962052.autores: Jin H, Wang Z, … Xia X (31 autores)
42962052.resumo: Trained immunity is tightly regulated by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming, yet how these changes are orchestrated at the chromatin level to establish long-term innate immune memory is not fully understood. Here, we show that induction of trained immunity elevates nuclear levels of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), which directly binds to KDM5A demethylase and inhibits its activity, thereby sustaining H3K4me3 (histone H3 lysine 4 trimethylation) levels and chromatin accessibility at inflammatory gene promoters to enhance "memory" responsiveness upon restimulation. Genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), the rate-limiting enzyme for NAD+ synthesis, impaired trained immunity and associated antitumor activity. Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) supplementation rescued defective trained immunity-mediated antitumor activity in NAMPT-deficient and aged mice. In human cancer, NAMPT expression in myeloid cells correlated with an inflammatory tumor microenvironment. Our findings identify KDM5A as a nuclear NAD+ sensor that orchestrates histone methylation and chromatin accessibility required for trained immunity.

42956059.titulo: Synthetic auxotrophy reveals metabolic regulation of plasma cell generation, affinity maturation, and cytokine receptor signaling.
42956059.autores: Cho SH, Brookens SK, … Boothby MR (17 autores)
42956059.resumo: The proliferation and development of activated B lymphocytes into antibody (Ab)-secreting plasma cells are critical determinants of humoral immunity and sustain certain autoimmune diseases. Specific pathways and substrate supplies in intermediary metabolism influence lymphocyte differentiation and function. We now show that although stringent restriction of glutamine supply decreases B cell proliferation and differentiation into plasma cells, glutaminolysis - a major metabolic use of this amino acid - was only conditionally crucial in B cells and the Ab responses derived from them. Gls, the gene encoding the main glutaminase of lymphocytes, promoted anti-NP Ab responses at the primary and recall phases if either glucose uptake into mouse B cells or pyruvate into their mitochondria was also impaired. Otherwise, it was dispensable. This synthetic auxotrophy, that is, the conditional requirement of glutaminase for processes in addition to survival, involved supporting progressive expansion of mitochondrial respiration followed by plasma cell differentiation. Surprisingly, impairment of glutaminase and the mitochondrial pyruvate channel decreased IL-21 stimulation of STAT3 phosphorylation as well as interferon stimulation of STAT1 activation. Together, our findings establish a powerful collaboration of metabolic pathways in programming increased respiration and the development of Ab-secreting cells, but also reveal modulation of cytokine receptor signaling by metabolism.

42955323.titulo: Immunological signatures of sepsis in abdominal solid organ transplant recipients: A multilayer and multicentric prospective cohort study.
42955323.autores: Witowski A, Bracht T, … Koos B (30 autores)
42955323.resumo:
Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection. Patients with prior abdominal solid organ transplantation (SOT) are highly susceptible to infection due to chronic immunosuppression, yet exhibit improved survival once sepsis occurs. The underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
We conducted a post hoc analysis within a prospective multicenter cohort of septic patients (SepsisDataNet.NRW; n = 538). Clinical outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. Immune profiling included serum cytokines, flow cytometric immunophenotyping, plasma proteomics, and intracellular signaling using proximity ligation assays (PLA) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). To reduce clinical confounding, complementary exploratory analyses were performed in a non-septic kidney transplant cohort (e:KID).
SOT patients demonstrated improved 30-day survival compared with non-SOT patients (84% vs. 66%; adjusted HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.26-0.95). Cytokine analysis revealed lower IL-6 and TNF-α levels alongside higher IL-18 concentrations, indicating an altered inflammatory profile. Flow cytometry showed reductions in adaptive immune cells but relatively preserved innate immune function, reflected by higher monocytic HLA-DR expression. Proteomics identified enrichment of innate immune, complement, and lipid metabolic response networks. PLA-based cellular analyses revealed increased GLUT1 expression and enhanced TFAM/TFB2M interaction in SOT patients, indicating a distinct immunometabolic marker profile. In e:KID patients paired serum metabolomics demonstrated higher glucose and lower lactate concentrations 12 months after transplantation, accompanied by broader alterations in lipid and branched-chain amino acid profiles.
In patients with sepsis, abdominal SOT is associated with significant better survival than in non-SOT patients. Septic abdominal SOT patients display a distinct immune phenotype characterized by attenuated systemic inflammation, relative preservation of selected innate immune readouts, and alterations in immunometabolic markers.

42959336.titulo: Gut bacterial lauroyl tryptamine reduces GPR183-associated inflammatory responses in human macrophages and T cells in vitro.
42959336.autores: Lezzerini M, Spek V, … Zhang J (10 autores)
42959336.resumo:
Recent research has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in producing bioactive metabolites that interact with G-protein coupled receptors (GPRs) and influence immune responses. Lauroyl tryptamine (LT), a metabolite produced by Agathobacter rectalis (formerly Eubacterium rectale), has been reported to antagonize GPR183, a receptor implicated in inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD). LT inhibits the binding of GPR183 with its natural ligands 7a,25-dihydroxycholesterol (OHC).
Here, we analyzed the GPR183 gene expression in intestinal tissues from IBD patients and non-IBD controls, as well as our previous single-cell transcriptomic dataset to identify key GPR183-expressing cells. We then use in vitro THP-1 derived macrophage and Jurkat T cell culture to test the effects of LT on inflammatory responses.
The GPR183 gene expression is elevated specifically in colonic and rectal tissues of ulcerative colitis patients, but not in Crohn's disease or ileal tissue. By analyzing single-cell transcriptomic dataset, we identified monocytes/macrophages, T cells, B cells, and innate lymphoid cells as key GPR183-expressing populations in human intestine. Using cell culture models, we demonstrated that LT modulates inflammatory pathways. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, OHC increased transcription of pro-inflammatory genes IL6, TNFA, and IL1B, which are reduced by LT. In activated Jurkat T cells, LT slightly decreased the OHC-mediated increase in the transcription of IL2. These findings support the hypothesis that LT, a known GPR183 antagonist, could modulate GPR183-associated inflammation in human macrophages and T cells in a context- and cell type-dependent manner, offering potential mechanistic insights into bioactive metabolite-mediated host-microbiota interactions in human intestine.

42953363.titulo: New strategies for the treatment of tuberculosis: research progress and clinical translation in immune modulation and inflammation control.
42953363.autores: Du S, Zhen L, … Deng D (4 autores)
42953363.resumo: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global public health challenge, with treatment complicated by drug resistance, adverse effects, and suboptimal host immune responses. Whilst conventional anti-TB drugs are effective bactericidally, their immunomodulatory effects may, in certain contexts, contribute to immune imbalance and affect treatment outcomes. Host-directed therapy (HDT), which aims to modulate the host immune response to enhance pathogen control and limit immunopathology, has emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy. This narrative review critically evaluates the current evidence for HDT in TB, focusing on immunosenescence, trained immunity, cytokine and lipid mediator networks, immunometabolic reprogramming, neuroendocrine regulation, and repurposed drugs including metformin and statins. Importantly, we distinguish between evidence derived directly from TB models (in vitro, animal, and clinical studies) and evidence extrapolated from other diseases, highlighting knowledge gaps and areas requiring further investigation. We propose that future progress depends on evidence-based stratification of HDT candidates, rigorous clinical trial design, and a personalised approach that accounts for patient comorbidities and immune status. This review aims to provide a balanced framework for advancing HDT from bench to bedside in TB therapy.

42953047.titulo: VZV reactivation, immune remodeling, and dementia risk.
42953047.autores: Zhang L, Wu S, … Yao W (4 autores)
42953047.resumo: Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV) is a highly dermatotropic and neurotropic α-herpesvirus that causes varicella (chickenpox) during primary infection, subsequently establishing lifelong latency, and reactivates to cause herpes zoster when host immunity declines or suppressed. Recent large-scale epidemiological studies consistently associate herpes zoster immunization, particularly with the recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV), with a significantly reduced risk of incident dementia. These findings have prompted a rigorous re-evaluation of the infectious etiology of progressive neurodegeneration. This review integrates the intersecting molecular mechanisms of VZV latency, localized ganglionic immunosenescence, and systemic inflammaging. We critically evaluate a synergistic VZV-HSV-1 amyloidogenic cascade, while explicitly addressing the biological limitations of extrapolating these transient interactions to human central nervous system (CNS) neuropathology. Furthermore, we propose the hypothesis that AS01B-induced trained immunity may contribute to neuroprotection. Therefore, this review provides insight for understanding the systemic consequences of chronic VZV infection and the impact of adjuvant-mediated immune remodeling in aging populations.

42952699.titulo: Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers persistent hepatic immunometabolic remodeling following SARS-CoV-2 infection in obese hosts.
42952699.autores: Qian W, Wei X, … Hahn YS (8 autores)
42952699.resumo: SARS-CoV-2 infection affects multiple organs, and chronic post-viral tissue injury is often associated with persistent immune dysregulation. Obesity and related metabolic disorders are major risk factors for severe COVID-19 and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), including liver dysfunction. To define hepatic responses during post-acute infection, we studied lean and diet-induced obese mice at 7 and 28 days following infection with mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2. Compared with lean mice, obese mice exhibited persistent lung inflammation and fibrosis, along with liver injury characterized by increased lipid accumulation, cellular apoptosis, and metabolic dysfunction. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed obesity-associated alterations in hepatic immune and metabolic programs during post-acute infection. In particular, hepatic macrophages in obese mice showed sustained inflammatory and metabolic transcriptional alterations, while hepatocytes displayed altered programs associated with gluconeogenesis and lipid metabolism. Endothelial cells also exhibited persistent transcriptional changes linked to immune activation and prothrombotic pathways. These alterations remained evident at 28 days post-infection, suggesting incomplete restoration of immune and metabolic homeostasis in obese liver. Collectively, our findings reveal persistent obesity-associated hepatic immunometabolic remodeling following SARS-CoV-2 infection and identify cellular and molecular programs that may contribute to post-acute liver sequelae in metabolically compromised hosts.

42956361.titulo: 7-(Chloroquinolin-4-yl) Sulfanyl Derivatives, Optimization of the Synthesis, In Silico ADMET Profiling Studies, and Evaluation of the Biological Activity Against Leishmania mexicana.
42956361.autores: Gelvez A, Labrador-Fagúndez L, … Benaim G (14 autores)
42956361.resumo: Leishmaniasis is a parasitic human infection that constitutes a major global health challenge due to limited therapeutic options, toxicity, resistance, and high costs of the drugs approved as therapy. In this study, a group of 7-chloroquinoline derivatives (5-12) was synthesized via an optimized route and evaluated against the human parasite Leishmania mexicana. Compounds were fully characterized and showed favorable in silico ADME/Tox profiles, including high predicted gastrointestinal absorption (>93%), although limited solubility and potential hepatotoxicity were observed for several derivatives. Biological assays demonstrated significant antileishmanial activity. Interestingly, intracellular amastigote assays revealed nanomolar potency and very high selectivity index (SI), with compound 12 exhibiting IC50 = 2.5 nM (SI = 21.030) and compound 9 IC50 = 5.2 nM (SI = 7.384). Mechanistic studies demonstrated concentration-dependent mitochondrial membrane depolarization and acidocalcisome alkalinization. Since these two organelles are both involved in bioenergetics and in parasite intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis, the results support the notion that intracellular Ca2+ disruption is an essential target for different drug actions. Overall, these findings support a multitarget mechanism and position these quinoline derivatives as promising chemical scaffolds for the development of improved antileishmanial strategies.

42963474.titulo: "Frozen" chromatin: insights on its structuring from cryo-EM tomography.
42963474.autores: Golyshev S, Kazakov E, Kireev I
42963474.revista: Chromosome research : an international journal on the molecular, supramolecular and evolutionary aspects of chromosome biology
42963474.resumo: Chromatin is a DNA-protein polymer that ensures the safekeeping and realization of genetic information in eukaryotic cells. The genome of higher eukaryotes is packed into a relatively small nuclear volume and organized in a non-random yet non-deterministic manner, exhibiting a high degree of complexity and flexibility. Despite the dense packing of chromatin, the cell effectively controls transcription, replication, and DNA repair. Genomic approaches, direct visualization, and computer modeling have allowed to accumulate a large amount of data on the structure and behavior of chromatin in various functional states. However, many of these techniques rely on chemical cross-linking, membrane permeabilization, or altered ionic conditions, which may perturb native chromatin structure. This has led to contradictory views on chromatin organization in situ. Cryo-electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) ensures preservation of the cellular structures in a close to native hydrated state and provides high resolving power, thus becoming a tool of choice for studying organization of chromatin at the nucleosomal and supranucleosomal scales. This review summarizes how cryo-EM has advanced our understanding of chromatin organization and function, considers the limitations of the method, and discusses future directions and perspectives in the field.

42956858.titulo: Inhibiting apolipoprotein C3 alleviates ferroptosis and cell damage induced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
42956858.autores: Liu Y, Yang X, … Yu J (7 autores)
42956858.resumo:
To explore the induction effect of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) infection on ferroptosis and inflammatory response in human hepatoma cells (Hep3B) and the regulatory effect of apolipoprotein C3(APOC3) on ferroptosis sensitivity.
Hep3B hepatocytes (MOI=5, 10, 15) were infected with the wild standard strain of PA (PAO1) for 4 h, 8 h, and 12 h respectively, and the survival rate of cells under different infection concentrations and times was detected by CCK-8. The morphological changes of cells were observed under an inverted microscope to determine the infection conditions. After adding ferroptosis inhibitors or siRNA respectively to inhibit the expression of APOC3, lipid droplets were labeled using oil red O staining, and the formation of lipid droplets was observed under an inverted microscope. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) were detected using a fluorescent probe (DCFH-DA), and lipid peroxidation levels were detected using a microplate reader. The expression levels of Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor α (PPARα), APOC3 and related inflammatory factors were detected by RT-qPCR. The protein expression levels of APOC3 and the ferroptosis-related proteins SLC7A11 and ACSL4 were evaluated by Western blotting. The morphological changes of mitochondria in cells were observed by transmission electron microscopy. The content of Fe2+ in cells was detected using a divalent iron ion probe.
With the increase of infection concentration and the extension of time, the survival rate of Hep3B cells significantly decreased after PAO1 infection, and the cell morphology gradually changed from spindle-shaped to round and accompanied by fragmentation. The number of red lipid droplets within the cells increased with the increase of the bacterial load. The fluorescence intensity of ROS was enhanced. The expression of PPARα mRNA was down-regulated and the expression of APOC3 mRNA was up-regulated. The volume of mitochondria decreased, the membrane density increased, and the cristae were reduced or even disappeared. Western blotting further confirmed the changes in APOC3 protein expression and ferroptosis-related proteins, including SLC7A11 and ACSL4, following PAO1 infection and APOC3 knockdown. The intracellular lipid peroxidation level was significantly increased. Compared with the control group, the levels of IL-6 and TNF-α significantly increased after PA infection. After inhibiting the expression of APOC3, the expression level of ROS decreased, lipid peroxidation reduced, the number of lipid droplets decreased, the content of Fe2+ decreased, mitochondrial damage decreased, and the expression of ferroptosis-related factors decreased.
After the action of PA, cell activity significantly decreased, intracellular ROS generation increased, and intracellular lipid peroxidation was enhanced, leading to cell damage and death. Meanwhile, APOC3, as a key downstream target of PPARα, PA promotes the generation of APOC3 by inhibiting the expression of PPARα, and APOC3 reduces the hydrolysis of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins (TRL), thereby promoting lipid droplet formation. It causes the accumulation of lipids within cells. However, the continuous inhibitionof APOC3 can reverse this effect. That is, after PA infects cells, it can promote the increase of APOC3 expression, leading to lipid metabolism disorders, and APOC3 plays a promoting role in the process of PA promoting ferroptosis in cells.

42955202.titulo: Sustainable synthesis of metallic nanoparticles and their potential biotechnological applications.
42955202.autores: Ugale SV, Gaikwad SC, … Nawani N (4 autores)
42955202.resumo: Nanotechnology has emerged as a vital interdisciplinary field with applications in medicine, biotechnology, environmental remediation, agriculture, energy, and advanced materials. Metallic nanoparticles (NPs), typically ranging from 1 to 100 nm, have distinctive physicochemical characteristics, including small size, a high surface-area-to-volume ratio, surface reactivity, and tunable electronic properties. Although conventional physical and chemical methods can effectively control nanoparticle (NP) composition and morphology, they may require high energy inputs, specialized equipment, or potentially toxic reagents. Therefore, biological synthesis strategies using plants, microorganisms, and biologically derived molecules have received much attention as alternative approaches for metallic NP synthesis.This review critically evaluates conventional, biological, and hybrid strategies for synthesizing metallic NPS, with particular emphasis on silver (Ag), copper (Cu), and silver-copper (Ag-Cu) bimetallic nanomaterials. The review also discusses NP's characterization methods, including UV-Visible (UV-Vis) spectroscopy, Electron microscopy (EM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta-potential analysis, and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), while emphasizing the limitations of interpreting any single technique in isolation. This work highlights the transition from laboratory-scale green synthesis to reproducible, scalable nanomanufacturing, including challenges associated with batch-to-batch reproducibility, biological-feedstock variability, purification, process control, safety, toxicity, and life-cycle sustainability. Finally, the review highlights the diverse biotechnological applications of metallic NPs in antimicrobial systems, diagnostics, drug delivery, agriculture, environmental remediation, and related industrial sectors. Overall, the review argues that biological synthesis methods should not automatically be regarded as sustainable. Instead, assess their advantages by integrating material performance, process efficiency, reproducibility, scalability, safety, and environmental impact.

42958614.titulo: Molecular Packaging, Liquid-Crystalline Order, and Three-Dimensional Architecture of Dinoflagellate Chromosomes.
42958614.autores: Chung JM, Suzaki T, … Song C (4 autores)
42958614.resumo: Many dinoflagellates package exceptionally large nuclear genomes within the dinokaryon, a nucleus that departs from conventional eukaryotic patterns of chromosome condensation, DNA packaging, and mitosis. Their chromosomes remain visibly condensed through most or all of the cell cycle. In many core dinoflagellates, DNA exhibits cholesteric liquid-crystalline order, while canonical nucleosomal chromatin does not serve as the dominant structural framework. This review synthesizes current evidence on dinoflagellate chromosome organization, spanning molecular packaging mechanisms and three-dimensional nuclear architecture. Dinoflagellates are histone-poor rather than histone-free: divergent core histones persist at low abundance, whereas HCc/MBNP-type proteins can be highly abundant in some species, with additional contributions from dinoflagellate viral nucleoproteins, divalent cations, RNA-associated factors, and modified DNA bases. Classical electron microscopy revealed nested arch patterns consistent with cholesteric order and inspired spiral, double-helical, and toroidal chromonema models, although molecular-resolution support remains lacking and fixation-sensitive features require caution. Recent volume electron microscopy and chromosome-conformation studies are revising chromosome counts and nuclear organization. Each of four reconstructed Oxyrrhis marina nuclei contained 398-405 physically segmented chromosome bodies, focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) reconstruction of a Prorocentrum cordatum CCMP 1329 nucleus resolved 62 tightly packed chromosome bodies together with an organized nucleolus and clustered nuclear pores, and high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) studies in Symbiodiniaceae revealed chromosome-scale scaffolds and transcription-dependent domains. Integrating standardized volume electron microscopy, chromosome-scale genomics, cryo-electron tomography, and biochemical reconstitution should connect molecular packaging to whole-nucleus architecture and improve understanding of ecologically important microbial eukaryotes.

42963108.titulo: Conservation of a synaptic blueprint across the animal kingdom.
42963108.resumo: Chemical synapses are fundamental computational units of the nervous system that enable rapid and precise information transfer through the nanoscale organization of presynaptic and postsynaptic components. Despite hundreds of millions of years of animal evolution and extraordinary diversity in nervous system architectures, the core physiological principles of chemical synaptic transmission remain remarkably conserved. Studies across Drosophila melanogaster, zebrafish, Caenorhabditis elegans, frogs and mammals reveal recurring principles governing active-zone organization, synaptic vesicle exocytosis, calcium signalling and postsynaptic specialization. Here, we examine the evolution of chemical synapses across the animal kingdom, focusing on the relationship between molecular diversification, nanoscale organization and functional conservation. We propose that the evolutionary stability of synapses reflects, in part, a stringent biophysical constraint imposed by the requirements for rapid chemical communication. We further consider how these conserved synaptic operations are assembled into neural circuits of dramatically different complexities, as well as the ctenophore nervous system as a critical test case for distinguishing molecular conservation from architectural and functional convergence. Across species, the emerging picture is that evolution has adhered to conserving the geometry and organizational principles of chemical synapses more stringently than a precise molecular composition. Synapses thus represent stable yet adaptable information-processing architectures in which conserved nanoscale constraints coexist with molecular flexibility and extensive diversification of neural circuits.

42962658.titulo: Age-dependent structural evolution of a functional amyloid contributes to memory impairment in Drosophila.
42962658.autores: Ou S, Guillen-Poza PA, … Hervas R (15 autores)
42962658.resumo: Cryogenic electron microscopy has revealed endpoint structures of ex vivo amyloid filaments, but how amyloids assemble and evolve in living organisms-and how these transitions affect physiology-remains poorly understood. Here, we map the age-dependent structural landscape of Orb2 amyloid, a synaptic translation regulator required for long-term memory, across the adult lifespan of Drosophila melanogaster. By determining multiple Orb2 amyloid structures, we uncover a dynamic, age-linked progression of amyloid states. Translation-promoting assemblies predominate early in life, whereas aging shifts the Orb2 amyloid ensemble toward structurally distinct, destabilization-resistant assemblies with reduced translational activity, coinciding with memory impairment. Manipulating memory-related chaperones in the brain shifts Orb2 toward youthful, translation-promoting states and improves memory in old flies; conversely, shifting Orb2 toward aged-like, translation-deficient states in young adults is associated with premature memory impairment. These findings define an in vivo trajectory of amyloid evolution and link amyloid structural dynamics to synaptic translation and memory.

42961978.titulo: Glutamate receptor composition at Drosophila neuromuscular junctions depends on developmental stage and muscle identity.
42961978.autores: Sustar A, Qiu C, … Tuthill JC (5 autores)
42961978.resumo: The neuromuscular junction (NMJ) of larval Drosophila is widely used for studying synaptic transmission. Larval body wall muscles express five ionotropic glutamate receptor (iGluR) subunits that assemble into two tetrameric complexes, with subunit composition determining the strength and plasticity of synaptic transmission. Because NMJ function has been extensively characterized in larvae, it has commonly been assumed that adult fly NMJs share this molecular composition, despite substantial differences between life stages. Here, we systematically compare glutamate receptor expression across larval and adult Drosophila muscles. We find that adult leg and flight muscles exhibit different iGluR expression than larvae, lacking expression of several receptors previously considered essential. Adjacent muscles within the adult femur express distinct iGluRs, suggesting specialization of flexor and extensor muscles. Finally, the glutamate-gated chloride channel (GluClα) is expressed extrasynaptically in adult but not larval muscle fibers. Our results reveal unexpected heterogeneity in glutamate receptor expression across muscles and developmental stages, demonstrating the need for muscle-specific analyses in flies and other animals.

42958608.titulo: Advances in research on the regulation of honey bee odor and chemical communication by symbiotic microorganisms.
42958608.autores: Chen YJ, Wang YC, … Miao CH (11 autores)
42958608.resumo: Because honey bees are key pollinators in terrestrial ecosystems, they are highly sensitive to environmental changes, and colony survival serves as a reliable indicator of environmental conditions. Insect symbiotic microorganisms regulate host chemical communication through multiple pathways, thereby playing critical roles in pheromone synthesis, olfactory perception, and social behavior modulation. However, a systematic review of the potential regulatory mechanisms by which symbiotic microorganisms influence chemical communication in honey bees is still lacking. Here, we synthesize domestic and international research to assess the compositions of symbiotic microorganisms in honey bees, as well as the mechanisms of pheromone release, perception, and function. Furthermore, drawing on specific experimental cases, we discuss how honey bee symbionts modulate host sensitivity to chemical signals and consequently affect host social behavior through multiple routes. These pathways are involved in regulating odorant-binding protein or odorant receptor expression and nervous system function, altering cuticular hydrocarbon profiles, modulating olfactory memory, and mediating immune signaling. This review further explores the interplay between symbiotic microorganisms and the release and reception of chemical signals in honey bees, thereby providing a solid foundation for the conservation of endangered pollinating insects.

42951971.titulo: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
42951971.autores: Pugliese SM, Chou GM, … Brunton BW (7 autores)
42951971.resumo: Animal locomotion relies on rhythmic body movements driven by central pattern generators (CPGs): neural circuits that produce oscillating output without oscillating input. However, the circuit structure of a CPG for walking is not known in any animal1,2. To identify the cells and synapses that underlie rhythmic leg movement in walking flies, we developed dynamic simulations of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord connectomes3-6. A computational activation screen of descending neurons from the central brain identified DNg100-a known command neuron for walking-as the strongest driver of rhythmic leg motor activity. Simulated network pruning isolated a minimal rhythm-generating circuit consisting of one inhibitory and two excitatory interneurons; this three-neuron circuit was necessary and sufficient for motor rhythms across all six legs and in four connectome datasets. Simulations also predicted that a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies. Our results reveal the cellular identity and synaptic structure of a putative CPG circuit for walking and other rhythmic leg movements in flies.

42960179.titulo: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-out of abnormal chemosensory jump 6 (acj6) gene impacts Helicoverpa armigera antennal lobe structure.
42960179.autores: Xie G, Chen S, … Zhao X (9 autores)
42960179.resumo: The specificity of the olfactory system in the brain is determined not only by the expression of odorant receptor genes but also by the specific neural circuit assembly within the antennal lobe (AL). To investigate the developmental role of abnormal chemosensory jump 6 (acj6) in the moth Helicoverpa armigera, we generated Haacj6 mutants using CRISPR/Cas9 and examined the detailed structure of the AL based on immunostaining and three-dimensional reconstruction. The results showed that the AL in male Haacj6 mutants was markedly enlarged. In both sexes, the AL of Haacj6 mutants contained approximately 100 glomeruli, compared with about 75 glomeruli in wild-type. Glomerular volumes were also more heterogeneous in the mutants: the largest glomeruli were expanded, whereas the smallest were reduced, although the mean glomerular volume remained unchanged. These results demonstrate that the Haacj6 gene plays a critical role in normal AL development and that AL enlargement in the mutants arises primarily from the presence of additional glomeruli. These additional glomeruli likely reflect defects in olfactory receptor neuron axon wiring to AL projection neurons, or glial mediated glomerular boundary formation. These findings indicate that acj6 is an essential regulator of AL architecture and provide crucial insights into the molecular mechanisms governing neural circuits assembly in insects.

42957696.titulo: Clock neurons modulate seizure timing through a diurnal switch.
42957696.autores: Cuddapah VA, Hsu CT, … Sehgal A (9 autores)
42957696.resumo: People with epilepsy experience daily oscillations in seizure risk. Using a video-tracking model to automate detection, we explored mechanisms underlying spontaneous seizures in Drosophila and find that flies, like people, exhibit daily oscillations in seizure risk. These rhythms are absent in flies lacking a molecular circadian clock and are independent of sleep. Thermogenetic screening and cell-specific clock perturbations reveal that the ventrolateral neurons, including "morning cells", and dorsolateral neurons, comprising the "evening cells", modulate diurnal oscillations in seizure risk. Pigment-dispersing factor and short neuropeptide F from morning cells increase seizure risk during the day. During this time, morning cell activity increases whole-brain activity. At night, morning cells switch to glycine signaling likely acting on evening cells to decrease seizure risk. Optogenetic inhibition of clock neurons suppresses seizure risk. Our findings reveal an unexpected role for brain clock neurons in modulating daily seizure risk.
